ImageContent.Description: Two grey wolves move through the sagebrush of Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming, home to some of North America's most closely watched wolf packs. Their thick coats help them withstand harsh winters, and their keen senses make them skilled hunters and communicators.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Two grey wolves, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, United States

ImageContent.Description: Few places in South Korea capture the magic of autumn quite like Naejangsan National Park, where mountainsides glow in brilliant shades of scarlet, orange, yellow and gold. Located in the country's southwest, the park is particularly famous for its vivid maple colours, making it one of Korea's premier destinations for autumn scenery. Its name, meaning 'many secrets in the mountains,' reflects the varied landscapes found throughout the region.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Autumn in Naejangsan National Park, South Korea

ImageContent.Description: Bridging the gap between old and new, Nguyen Hoang Bridge gives Hue's skyline a fresh connection. Spanning the Perfume River in Vietnam, the modern steel-arch landmark opened to traffic on March 26, 2025. Its design, called 'The Crane Facing Thien Mu,' draws inspiration from a local legend and nearby Thien Mu Pagoda.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Nguyen Hoang Bridge over the Perfume River, Hue, Vietnam

ImageContent.Description: Slow and steady wins the race—and the brown-throated sloth seems perfectly happy to skip the race altogether. This three-toed mammal has a different approach to life: conserve energy, hang on and take your time.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Brown-throated sloth, Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, Costa Rica

ImageContent.Description: What if a city's busiest street had no road? In Venice, Italy, traffic flows along the Grand Canal, a 3.8-kilometre waterway that winds through the city in a giant reverse S-shape. Known to locals as the Canalazzo, it is Venice's main water-traffic corridor, carrying vaporetti, water taxis, gondolas, police boats and other vessels. The canal follows the course of an ancient river that once flowed into the Venetian Lagoon.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Grand Canal in Venice, Italy

ImageContent.Description: If parks could keep birthday diaries, Eryri National Park (Snowdonia) in Wales would have quite the story to tell. The park turns 75 today, marking the anniversary of its designation in 1951. Eryri stretches across 2,130 square kilometres, with nine mountain ranges, 119 kilometres of coastline and habitats ranging from peatlands and native woodlands to upland landscapes. At more than 1,050 metres, Yr Wyddfa is Eryri's highest point. Nearby, the Carneddau and Glyderau add their own peaks, while Cadair Idris rises in the south. These protected landscapes provide habitats for wildlife and include 17 National Nature Reserves and 56 Sites of Special Scientific Interest.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Dolbadarn Castle, Llanberis, Eryri National Park (Snowdonia), Wales

ImageContent.Description: Perugia has a walkway with a story beneath every step: its medieval aqueduct. Construction began in 1254, and by around 1280, the aqueduct was carrying water from Monte Pacciano to the Fontana Maggiore in the city centre. The clever bit? Engineers found a way to make the water flow uphill. Using a pressurised conduit, the system overcame the city's steep terrain—an impressive feat of medieval engineering.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Medieval Aqueduct, Perugia, Italy

ImageContent.Description: Winter brings a familiar rhythm to Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico. The cranes arrive, wetlands fill with birds and this area becomes a hub for seasonal wildlife. Established in 1939, the 57,331-acre sanctuary was created to provide a protected stopover for migrating waterfowl. Its wetlands, fields and waterways now support wildlife throughout the year. Sandhill cranes, seen in today's image, are especially associated with the refuge during winter.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Sandhill cranes, Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge, New Mexico, USA

ImageContent.Description: As morning mist drifts among the standing stones of Avebury in Wiltshire, England, the scene feels almost timeless. These ancient megaliths form part of one of the world's most remarkable prehistoric landscapes, centred on a vast Neolithic monument built around 4,500 years ago. Avebury contains the world's largest prehistoric stone circle, as well as a massive henge and stone avenues extending into the surrounding countryside. Together with nearby monuments such as Silbury Hill and West Kennet Avenue, it forms part of an extensive Neolithic complex that has fascinated generations of visitors, researchers and archaeologists.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England

ImageContent.Description: What stories could these walls tell? Rising above eastern Bohemia in Czechia, Kunětická hora Castle has witnessed centuries of history. Dating to the late 14th century, the castle gradually evolved into an impressive fortress and noble residence. Its elevated position offered commanding views of the surrounding countryside and helped make it an important stronghold.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia

ImageContent.Description: Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the south-eastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: A grove of pond cypress trees with autumn foliage, Georgia, United States

ImageContent.Description: In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria

ImageContent.Description: When night falls in Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada, the mountains get a whole new backdrop. Designated a Dark-Sky Preserve in 2011, the park spans more than 11,000 square kilometres, with measures in place to reduce light pollution. Here, the stars, planets and the Milky Way put up a celestial show, giving visitors a reason to look up. Then morning arrives and the focus shifts from the sky above to the landscape below.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Maligne Lake, Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada

ImageContent.Description: In much of Brazil, July is synonymous with cold weather, mist and muted tones. The green-headed tanager goes in the opposite direction. Green, blue, turquoise, yellow, black, orange and touches of violet come together on a body just over 13 centimetres long, appearing among the branches like a living argument for extravagance. It is no surprise that it frequently features on lists of the most beautiful birds in the world.
ImageContent.Headline: Info
ImageContent.Title: Green-headed tanager
